issues.legal_issue: A binding charge on property securing income set aside for religious charities can constitute a specific endowment even though the owners retain title to the property.
material_facts: The settlement deed charged the properties with payment of specified amounts for eleven charities found to be religious in nature.
The owners retained the properties and the balance of their income, but the charities could enforce payment and the charge.
The owners challenged an administrative declaration that the provision for the charities was a specific endowment.
issues.conclusion: A specific endowment was created in respect of the right to receive the amounts set aside for the eleven religious charities; transfer of title to the properties was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 6(14) and 6(16) of the Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951, religious and specific endowments include partial as well as absolute dedications. Section 32 contemplates a specific endowment consisting merely of a charge on property. A binding charge that divests the owners of the right to the charged income may therefore constitute an endowment; it need not first be transferred to a separate person. This approach is supported by Iswari Bhubaneshwari v. Brojo Nath Dey and Mayne's Hindu Law, Eleventh Edition, p. 923.

predicates.proceeding_challenges_endowment_classifi: A proceeding challenges a determination that property or income is an endowment for religious or charitable purposes.
predicates.binding_charge_created: The persons controlling property made a legally enforceable charge on it to secure payment for a stated purpose.
predicates.income_reserved_for_religious_charities: A portion of income from the charged property was set aside for religious charities.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges an endowment classification and a binding charge secures income reserved for religious charities, the outcome is that a specific endowment is created.

issues.legal_issue: A deed specifying amounts for particular charities creates an endowment of those sums, rather than a percentage of the property income, merely because income and expenses later increase.
material_facts: The deed listed amounts for the charities, totaling Rs. 1,590 for the eleven religious charities at issue.
Some amounts were described as approximate, and one provision stated a quantity of grain with an approximate cost.
The property's income and the charities' expenses had increased since the deed was made.
The High Court treated the endowment as 15.9 per cent of the property's income, and that characterization was challenged.
issues.conclusion: The endowment was the right to receive the specified total sum from the property income, subject to the owners' discretion to make slight variations; it was not a percentage of the income.
issues.legal_principle: The instrument must be interpreted according to the amounts it specifies. Subsequent increases in income and expenditure do not change the instrument's meaning, and the use of approximate amounts permits only slight variation rather than creating a right to a proportion of income.

rule.if: proceeding_challenges_endowment_quantum and deed_specifies_charity_sums and later_income_and_expenses_increased and approximate_wording_in_some_items

predicates.proceeding_challenges_endowment_quantum: A proceeding contests how much income or property was dedicated to specified charities.
predicates.deed_specifies_charity_sums: The instrument establishing the charitable provision states amounts for particular charities.
predicates.later_income_and_expenses_increased: The property's income and the expenses of the charities increased after the instrument was made.
predicates.approximate_wording_in_some_items: The instrument describes some specified amounts or their costs as approximate.

issues.definition: When a proceeding contests the quantum of an endowment created by specified charity sums, later increases in income and expenses and approximate wording in some items lead to an outcome limited to those specified sums with slight variation.
